AgentUpgradeResource.description:
A staged self-upgrade of the agent with automatic rollback.

The agent downloads and verifies the new binary, keeps the running one as the
previous version, swaps, and restarts. The new agent must complete `hello` and
report this resource `applied` within `health_timeout_seconds`; otherwise the
previous binary is restored and the resource reports `failed` / `rolled_back`.

version.description: Version string as its upstream publishes it, for example 26.7.11 or v2.9.6.

NginxArtifactResource.description:
A set of nginx files applied as one unit.

The agent writes every file, runs `nginx -t`, and reloads. If the test or the
reload fails it restores the previous files, reloads again, and reports the
resource `failed` with `validation_failed` or `reload_failed`.

ServiceSignature.description:
Ed25519 signature by the control service's signing key.

The key's certificate is issued by the fleet's pinned internal CA and reaches
the agent in `EnrollResponse` and `HelloResponse`. The agent verifies the
signature before acting, so a TLS interception or a self-signed fallback
certificate on 443 can never inject desired state or commands.

key_id.description: SHA-256 of the DER signing certificate that made the signature.
key_id.title: Key Id

signature.description: Ed25519 signature (64 bytes) in standard base64.
signature.title: Signature

XrayConfigResource.description:
The Xray configuration, validated with `xray run -test` before it replaces the old file.

Inbounds whose users come from `xray_users` or `hysteria2_users` resources keep
an empty `settings.clients` list here. The agent adds users through Xray's gRPC
API and also writes them into those `clients` lists on disk (without a restart),
so a reboot never loses a user. A change to this resource restarts Xray through
the systemd unit that lists it in `restart_on`.

api_address.description: Loopback address of the Xray gRPC API inbound declared in `config`.
api_address.title: Api Address

config.description: Xray JSON configuration object, without managed users.
config.title: Config

description:
Everything one node should run, as one signed document.

The agent refuses a document whose `fleet_epoch` is below the highest it has
accepted, whose (fleet_epoch, revision) is below the one it holds, or that
repeats a held (fleet_epoch, revision) with a different `sha256`. Equal
`sha256` means equal content, so a new revision with the same hash only
records the new revision.

fleet_epoch.description: Fleet epoch. A restore of the control service bumps it. An agent remembers the highest epoch it accepted and refuses desired state and commands from an older one (a resurrected old control server).
fleet_epoch.title: Fleet Epoch

fleet_id.description: Fleet identifier: a lowercase UUID fixed when the fleet is created.
fleet_id.title: Fleet Id

issued_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, ending in Z.
issued_at.title: Issued At

node_id.description: Node identifier: the server's lowercase topology ID, unique within the fleet.
node_id.title: Node Id

revision.description: Desired-state revision for one node. Ordering is (fleet_epoch, revision): within an epoch revisions only grow; a higher epoch wins even with a lower revision.
revision.title: Revision

sha256.description: Protocol hash of the `resources` array as sent (JCS, SHA-256).
sha256.title: Sha256

title: DesiredNodeState
